s: So you may have heard that the clean-energy transition has failed and that we should be pragmatic, which means accepting our almost complete and permanent dependence on fossil fuels.
所以你可能听说过,清洁能源过渡失败了,
And I'm here to tell you that is wrong.
我来告诉你这是错误的.
Now I’m also here to tell you that the transition, which is happening, will not look like this.
我也想告诉你们,正在发生的过渡将不会像这样.
If you think that the transition is going to be heralded by this dramatic reduction in fossil fuel use and in emissions, then I'm afraid that model has failed.
如果你认为过渡将由化石燃料使用和排放量大幅减少来预示,那么我担心这个模型失败了.
So let's look at how it might play out.
让我们看看它会如何发展.
And let's start with some data.
让我们从一些数据开始.
So this is electricity generation by source, the percentage, over the last 25 years.
这就是过去25年中发电的百分比.
And what you can see -- most dramatic -- is that green line.
你能看到的最戏剧性的就是绿色线.
It's called non-hydro renewables.
这被称为非水力可再生能源.
It's basically wind and solar.
这基本上是风能和太阳能.
And that now generates, those two sources of power, which were less than one percent 20 years ago, [and] now account for 20 percent of all global electricity.
现在,这两种电源, 20年前的电源不到1%,现在占全球所有电量的20%.
And that is despite the fact that demand has doubled over that period.
尽管在此期间需求增加了一倍.
So you’ve got solar doubling every three years.
所以每三年就有太阳能增加一倍.
You've got wind doubling every five years.
你的风每五年就翻了一番.
If you add those two together, they're about to overtake gas in the electricity mix.
如果把这两个加在一起,它们就会在电力混合物中赶上气体.
If you add hydro to those two, then they have already overtaken coal.
如果把水力添加到这两个,那么它们已经超过了煤炭.
So this is our first clean-energy miracle.
所以这是我们第一次清洁能源奇迹.
Now I want to talk about nuclear.
现在我想谈谈核.
I have a nuclear engineering background, and I think it's fantastic that we are now building new nuclear.
我有核工程学经验,我认为我们现在正在建造新的核能是很棒的.
And we've stopped shutting big nuclear plants.
我们已经停止关闭大型核电厂.
But we also have to be realistic.
但我们也必须要现实.
Here is wind and solar.
这里有风和太阳能.
Each of them has already overtaken the output of all the nuclear plants in the world.
它们已经超过了世界上所有核电站的产量.
So I think we should go ahead and build nuclear, but we need to do it in a clear-eyed way.
所以我认为我们应该继续建造核,但我们需要用清晰的眼睛去做.
Small modular reactors, if you want them to catch up with that green line that we've seen, you have to build not dozens, not hundreds, but thousands.
如果想让它们赶上我们看到的绿色线, 你必须建造不几十个,不几百个,而是数千个.
So now at this point, there’s usually some smart aleck who asks me, “Do I know that the sun doesn’t shine at night?”
现在,通常有人问我,我知道夜间太阳不发光吗?
And the polite version of my answer is yes.
我对这句话的礼貌是是.
But if you think that that means that that green line is going to stop curving upwards, well, here come batteries.
但如果你认为这意味着绿色线将停止向上曲线,
This is a forecast produced by the team that I recruited and built, which is now Bloomberg New Energy Finance, and this was their forecast from 2019.
这是我招募和构建的团队所制定的预测,现在是 ⁇ 博新能源金融,这是他们2019年的预测.
And it was for 25 percent compound growth in battery sales from then on.
从那时起,电池销量增长了25%.
What happened?
发生了什么事?
Forty-five percent compound growth.
总体增长为45%.
A doubling every two years.
每两年增加一倍.
And that is our second clean-energy miracle.
这是我们第二次清洁能源奇迹.
Now the naysayers will say, “All of this is irrelevant.
现在那些反驳者会说,
They don’t care about growth.”
他们不关心增长.
And they will say things like, "The share of hydrocarbons in the global primary energy mix has hardly budged from 85 percent in 1990 to 80 percent today."
他们会说:"全球初级能源组合中碳水化合物份额从1990年的85%下降到今天的80%.
Now what they don’t tell you is that that period spans Asia's incredible coal-fired growth.
但他们没有告诉你,这个时期跨越了亚洲的可怕的煤炭增长.
And what they won't talk about is the six oil-price crises that have damaged the economy so dramatically along the way.
他们不会谈论的就是这六次石油价格危机,
And the other thing they won't tell you is what is primary energy.
他们不会告诉你什么是原始能量.
So when people talk about primary energy, one of two things is happening.
所以当人们谈论初始能源时,
Either they don't know what they're talking about or they do know what they're talking about, but they hope that you don't.
他们不知道他们在谈论什么,或者他们知道他们在谈论什么,但他们希望你不知道.
Because primary energy is just what we shovel into the front end of our energy system.
因为原始能量就是我们把它 ⁇ 入能源系统前端的东西.
And over two-thirds of it goes to waste.
超过三分之二是浪费的.
Now it doesn’t go to waste because machines are inefficient.
机器是不高效的.
It goes to waste because every time you convert from fuel to heat and from heat to either mobility or electricity, the laws of thermodynamics say there will be waste.
因为每次你将燃料转换为热量,以及热量转换为移动或电力,热力学定律说,
What the economy uses is useful energy, energy at the point of use, delivering mobility and heating and lighting and air conditioning and so on.
经济使用的是有用的能源,在使用地点的能源,提供移动性,加热,照明,空调等.
So we need to understand what is delivering useful energy.
因此,我们需要了解提供有用的能量是什么.
Now it turns out there’s some new figures from the International Energy Agency that say 37 percent of it is actually electric.
国际能源署的新数据显示, 37%的能源实际上是电气的.
And around 30 percent of useful energy is already clean.
约30%的有用能源已经是清洁的.
So now armed with this knowledge, let's have a look at how the transition might actually play out.
让我们看看这种转型实际上是如何发生的.
And I built the world's smallest model of the entire global energy system to help us do that.
我建造了世界上最小的全球能源系统模型来帮助我们做到这一点.
It's four lines on a spreadsheet.
这是在电子表格上的四行.
Now it starts with the 30 percent clean energy, useful energy, of course.
现在,它从30%的清洁能源开始,当然是有用的能量.
The first line is the economy.
首先是经济.
It’s been growing at three percent per year, and we want it to continue.
我们希望它继续增长.
Pulling people out of poverty, improving lives.
让人们摆脱贫困,改善生活.
The second line is demand for useful energy.
第二条是对有用能源的需求.
That grows a little bit less fast because there’s energy efficiency -- we’ll call it two percent per year.
这种增长速度有点低,因为能源效率,我们会称之为每年2%.
Now clean energy supply, line three.
清洁能源供应,第三线.
It's been growing over five percent per year.
每年增长超过5%.
But I want to keep this really, really simple.
但我想保持这个非常,非常简单.
I'm just going to say five percent out into the future and let's see what happens.
我只会说 5% 进入未来,看看会发生什么.
Now the gap, what's left, is the bit we have to supply with fossil fuels until something better comes along.
剩下的差距是我们必须用化石燃料供应的部分,直到更好的东西出现.
And what you'll see is, for the first couple of decades, it doesn't get crushed.
你会看到,在前几十年里,它不会被 ⁇ 碎.
But after that, ... as clean energy grows faster than demand, the space available for fossil fuels gets reduced and they get forced off the system.
但之后,因为清洁能源比需求增长得更快,化石燃料的空间会减少,
Now look, there’s all sorts of terms and conditions here.
现在看,这里有各种条款和条件.
This is an illustration, and there'll be a long tail of difficult sectors and we may need to do some removal.
这是一个插图,将会有很长的困难部门的尾巴,
And this is only the energy system.
这只是能源系统.
It doesn't include land use or cow burps.
这不包括土地使用或牛 ⁇ .
But the beauty of this model is that it matches the way the world works.
但这个模型的美丽在于它与世界运作的方式相匹配.
So when we went from horses to cars, we didn't do it by banning horses.
所以,当我们从马变成汽车时,我们并没有禁止马.
We did it by building and selling cars, building.
我们通过建造和销售汽车,建造.
When we went from landlines to mobile digital telephony, we didn't do it by banning landlines.
当我们从固定电话转移到移动数字电话时,
We did it by building and selling mobile phones.
我们通过建造和销售手机来做到这一点.
Interestingly enough, in both of those cases, the old technology kept growing for around 30 years after the arrival of the new before collapsing.
值得注意的是,在这两种情况下,
So how do we keep clean energy growing faster than demand for the long term?
那么,我们如何让清洁能源长期增长速度比需求快?
First of all, keep growing supply, obviously.
首先,我们必须继续增加供应量.
And there, I think, we have a new superpower: superintelligence -- or as the rest of us call it, AI.
我认为,我们有一个新的超级大国:超级智能,或者我们所谓的AI.
But also we need to electrify much more of the economy, and that is happening.
但我们还需要更多地电气化经济,
So here you see cars.
这里你看到汽车.
Today globally, one car in three being sold is already electric.
今天全球销售的三辆汽车中就有一个是电动的.
It's two cars in three in China.
在中国,每三辆车就有两辆.
Fossil-fueled cars, sales of, peaked in 2017 and are already a third down.
化石燃料的汽车销量在2017年达到顶峰,已经下降了三分之一.
But it's not just cars.
但这不仅仅是汽车.
One heavy truck in China in three is already electric.
在中国,每3辆重型卡车中就有一个已经电动.
Now it's only one in 25 in Europe, but I'm trying to do something about that.
在欧洲,每25人中只有一个,但我正在努力做一些事情.
This is Europe's largest heavy-goods vehicle charging hub in Valencia, Spain, built by a company called PragmaCharge, which I chair.
这是欧洲最大的重货车充电中心,位于西班牙瓦伦西亚, 由我担任主席的PragmaCharge公司建造.
But it's not just transportation.
但这不仅仅是运输.
We're going to need another clean-energy miracle.
我们需要另一种清洁能源奇迹.
A third one.
第三个.
Hydrogen is not it.
⁇ 不是它.
It's electrification of heating.
这就是加热的电气化.
Already, one heating system in two is electric.
现在,每两种加热系统中一个是电动的.
It’s cheaper, it’s better, it’s healthier and it delivers air conditioning.
它更便宜,更好,更健康,提供空调.
And half of industrial heat is low-temperature, perfect for heat pumps.
工业热量的一半是低温的,
And even high-temperature industrial heat can be delivered electrically.
甚至高温的工业热量也可以通过电气来提供.
We will also need further clean-energy miracles.
我们还需要更多的清洁能源奇迹.
So we must keep going with deep-tech, hard-tech innovation.
因此,我们必须继续进行深度技术,硬技术创新.
And that will help with the outer years of the model.
这将有助于模型的外层.
But in summary, I am confident that we will get to a completely clean economy in due course, and we will do so for one simple reason.
但总之,我相信,我们将在适当的时间内实现一个完全清洁的经济,
Burning stuff is stupid.
燃烧东西是愚蠢的.
It's bad thermodynamics, it's bad economics, it's bad for people and planet, it's bad for security.
这对人类和地球有害,对安全有害.
So we will get there.
所以我们会到达那里.
There will be a transition.
这将是转型.
And by all means, let's be pragmatic.
让我们务实地思考.
But does being pragmatic mean accepting defeat and giving up?
但实践主义意味着接受失败并放弃?
Or does it mean leaning in and speeding up?
或是要倾斜并加快速度?
Because that is the choice we face.
因为这是我们面临的选择.
Thank you.
谢谢你.
